newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil trader Izui admits tax evasion - reports.
newsitem.headline: Oil trader Izui admits tax evasion - reports.

text.p: Japanese oil trader Junichiro Izui pleaded guilty to tax evasion charges at Tokyo District Court on Thursday, media reports said.
A further hearing was scheduled for Monday May 26 for Izui, who still faces charges of fraud and bribery.

The wealthy oil product wholesaler, arrested last November on suspicion of evading 330 million yen ($2.61 million) in income tax on oil trade commissions, was at the heart of an insider trading scandal which saw the resignation of two top Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd officials at the end of February.
Mitsubishi Oil was involved in unusual deals with Izui and is suspected of having paid a total of about 2.4 billion yen ($19.0 million) in questionable funds to the Osaka-based trader.

Last October, court papers in a legal dispute between Mitsubishi Oil and Mitsui Mining Co said Mitsubishi Oil had allegedly given the money to Izui through oil deals made between the companies from 1993 to 1995.

In February, the Trade Ministry revealed that a former ministry official approached power utilities about buying fuel oil from Mitsubishi Oil. The former official is believed to have acted on behalf of Izui, Jiji news agency reported.
The arrest of the Osaka-based oil dealer prompted a ministry survey which revealed that more than 100 bureaucrats had been wined and dined by Izui.
